question: A 19-year-old man consulted for a 24-hour history of pain, swelling and functional impotence of the right knee accompanied by a fever of 38ºC. Physical examination reveals inflammatory signs and joint effusion in the right knee. The analytical data show a leukocytosis with neutrophilia and an elevation of the C-reactive protein. The syndromic diagnosis of acute monoarthritis is made. What is the most likely etiologic diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Bacterial infectious arthritis -> Acute onset of pain, swelling, and functional impotence of the knee -> Fever of 38ºC -> Inflammatory signs and joint effusion on physical examination -> Leukocytosis with neutrophilia and elevated C-reactive protein -> Etiologic diagnosis of bacterial infectious arthritis -> 95%

CHAIN: Arthritis by microcrystals -> Acute onset of pain, swelling, and functional impotence of the knee -> Fever of 38ºC -> Inflammatory signs and joint effusion on physical examination -> Leukocytosis with neutrophilia and elevated C-reactive protein -> Etiologic diagnosis of arthritis by microcrystals -> 80%

CHAIN: Reactive arthritis -> Acute onset of pain, swelling, and functional impotence of the knee -> Fever of 38ºC -> Inflammatory signs and joint effusion on physical examination -> Leukocytosis with neutrophilia and elevated C-reactive protein -> Etiologic diagnosis of reactive arthritis -> 70%

CHAIN: Infectious arthritis due to mycobacteria -> Acute onset of pain, swelling, and functional impotence of the knee -> Fever of 38ºC -> Inflammatory signs and joint effusion on physical examination -> Leukocytosis with neutrophilia and elevated C-reactive protein -> Etiologic diagnosis of infectious arthritis due to mycobacteria -> 60%

CHAIN: Rheumatoid arthritis -> Chronic, symmetric polyarthritis -> Morning stiffness lasting more than 1 hour -> Etiologic diagnosis of rheumatoid arthritis unlikely in this acute monoarthritis presentation -> 20%
